title.en: Storytelling project: a story with a purpose

es: Escribir una historia de 220 a 270 palabras con gancho, tensión, giro, recursos de énfasis y una reflexión final.

teaching.en: A good hook puts the reader in the middle of a moment: I still remember the night I missed the last train.
teaching.es: Un buen gancho pone al lector en medio de un momento: Todavía recuerdo la noche en que perdí el último tren.
teaching.explanationEs: El gancho abre con un momento concreto, no con una explicación del tema.
segments: A good hook puts the reader in the middle of a
moment: I still remember the night I missed the last train.
teaching.audioText: A good hook puts the reader in the middle of a moment: I still remember the night I missed the last train.

teaching.en: Tension builds when the narrator gives a clue and delays the answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.
teaching.es: La tensión crece cuando el narrador da una pista y retrasa la respuesta: la estación estaba vacía y entonces oí pasos.
teaching.explanationEs: Clue + delay: primero la pista (empty, footsteps) y después, más tarde, la explicación.
segments: Tension builds when the narrator gives a clue and delays the
answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.
teaching.audioText: Tension builds when the narrator gives a clue and delays the answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.

teaching.en: The twist changes how we read the story: the stranger turned out to be my new teacher.
teaching.es: El giro cambia cómo leemos la historia: el desconocido resultó ser mi nuevo profesor.
teaching.explanationEs: Turn out to be = resultar ser: el giro revela algo que el lector no esperaba.
segments: The twist changes how we read the story: the
stranger turned out to be my new teacher.
teaching.audioText: The twist changes how we read the story: the stranger turned out to be my new teacher.

teaching.en: For emphasis, say 'It was the silence that frightened me' or 'Never had I felt so relieved'.
teaching.es: Para dar énfasis, di «Lo que me asustó fue el silencio» o «Nunca me había sentido tan aliviado».
teaching.explanationEs: Cleft: It was + lo destacado + that. Inversión: Never had I + participio. Úsalas una o dos veces.
segments: For emphasis, say 'It was the silence that frightened
me' or 'Never had I felt so relieved'.
teaching.audioText: For emphasis, say 'It was the silence that frightened me' or 'Never had I felt so relieved'.

teaching.en: Vivid details, such as the cold bench and the smell of coffee, make the scene real.
teaching.es: Los detalles vívidos, como el banco frío y el olor a café, hacen real la escena.
teaching.explanationEs: Vivid = muy gráfico: el detalle concreto vale más que un adjetivo general.
segments: Vivid details, such as the cold bench and
the smell of coffee, make the scene real.
teaching.audioText: Vivid details, such as the cold bench and the smell of coffee, make the scene real.

teaching.en: Looking back, I realise that my reflection at the end of the story was the most honest part.
teaching.es: Mirando atrás, me doy cuenta de que mi reflexión al final de la historia fue la parte más sincera.
teaching.explanationEs: Looking back, I realise… abre la reflexión: la lección que cambió tu forma de pensar.
segments: Looking back, I realise that my reflection at the
end of the story was the most honest part.
teaching.audioText: Looking back, I realise that my reflection at the end of the story was the most honest part.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es un gancho eficaz para abrir la historia?

choices.text: This story is about a train that I missed.
I still remember the night I missed the last train.
In this text, I will explain one night.

feedback.es: El gancho eficaz abre con un momento concreto («I still remember the night…»). Anunciar el tema con «This story is about…» no despierta curiosidad.

hint.es: Un gancho abre en un momento concreto; no anuncia el tema.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que me asustó fue el silencio.»

feedback.es: En la frase cleft con un nombre de cosa se usa that: It was the silence that frightened me.

hint.es: Con cosas, no con personas, la frase cleft usa este conector.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el giro de este fragmento?

choices.text: The platform was empty at midnight.
The narrator waited for the last train.
The man who followed the narrator turned out to be helping.

feedback.es: El giro revela que el hombre que parecía una amenaza en realidad ayudaba: cambia cómo entendemos todo lo anterior.

hint.es: El giro cambia el sentido de lo que el lector creía.

origin.text: I waited for the last train. The platform was empty, and a man followed me. He turned out to be the station guard, and he was carrying my lost wallet.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recurso crea tensión en este fragmento.

choices.text: A clue followed by a delay: footsteps with no explanation.
A twist that changes the whole story.
A reflection about what the narrator learned.

feedback.es: El narrador da una pista (pasos que se acercan) y no dice quién es: clue + delay crea tensión. No hay giro ni reflexión todavía.

origin.audio: The station was empty, and the clock showed midnight. Then I heard footsteps behind me, slowly coming closer.

prompt.es: ¿Qué final incluye una reflexión con propósito?

choices.text: And that was the end of my story about the train.
Looking back, I learned that asking for help is always a good idea.
The train left, and I went home.

feedback.es: «Looking back, I learned…» dice qué cambió en el narrador y por qué importa la historia. Las otras dos solo cierran los hechos.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué asustó más al narrador.

choices.text: The dark street itself.
The noise of the trains.
The silence of the city.

feedback.es: «It was not the dark that scared me, it was the silence»: la frase cleft descarta la oscuridad y destaca el silencio.

origin.audio: It was not the dark that scared me; it was the silence. The whole city was so quiet.

sentences: The man turned ___ to be my new teacher.
Looking back, I ___ that fear was the real problem.

prompt.es: Escribe tu historia de 220 a 270 palabras con gancho, tensión, giro, énfasis y reflexión.

answer.text: I still remember the night I missed the last train. I was a student, and I had spent the whole evening at a friend's birthday party in the next town. When I reached the station, the platform was empty and the clock showed midnight. My phone had no battery, and the nearest taxi was far away. I sat on a cold bench and tried to stay calm. It was not the dark that frightened me; it was the silence. Never had I heard a city so quiet. Then, behind me, I heard footsteps. They were slow, and they were coming closer. I held my bag tightly and did not look back. 'Are you waiting for the last train?' a voice asked. I looked up, and my heart stopped. The man in front of me was wearing a long grey coat, and he looked strangely familiar. He turned out to be Mr Duarte, my new science teacher, who lived two streets away. He smiled, offered me a lift and even gave me his phone charger. All the way home I kept thinking about how afraid I had been of a person who only wanted to help. Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.
accepted: I still remember the night I missed the last train. I was a student, and I had spent the whole evening at a friend's birthday party in the next town. When I reached the station, the platform was empty and the clock showed midnight. My phone had no battery, and the nearest taxi was far away. I sat on a cold bench and tried to stay calm. It was not the dark that frightened me; it was the silence. Never had I heard a city so quiet. Then, behind me, I heard footsteps. They were slow, and they were coming closer. I held my bag tightly and did not look back. 'Are you waiting for the last train?' a voice asked. I looked up, and my heart stopped. The man in front of me was wearing a long grey coat, and he looked strangely familiar. He turned out to be Mr Duarte, my new science teacher, who lived two streets away. He smiled, offered me a lift and even gave me his phone charger. All the way home I kept thinking about how afraid I had been of a person who only wanted to help. Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.

The night I missed the last train began like any other. I was at a party in the next town, and I left too late. On the platform, the clock showed midnight and nobody was there. I sat down and waited, because my phone had no battery. What frightened me most was the silence. Then I heard footsteps behind me, slow and close. I did not dare to look. The lights were weak, and the wind moved some old paper along the ground. A voice said, 'Are you waiting for the last train?' I looked up, and there was my new science teacher, Mr Duarte, in a long grey coat. It turned out that he lived nearby, and he offered me a lift home. In the car we hardly spoke, but it was warm, and the radio played softly. I felt almost ashamed. I had been afraid of a man who only wanted to help. Looking back, I learned that I often expect the worst when I am alone. Never again will I stay silent when I need help.

feedback.es: Una historia completa abre con un gancho concreto, da una pista y retrasa la respuesta, revela un giro, enfatiza una vez o dos y cierra con una reflexión.

origin.text: Tema: la noche en que perdiste el último tren. Datos: fiesta en otra ciudad; estación vacía a medianoche; el móvil sin batería; oyes pasos; el desconocido resulta ser tu nuevo profesor de ciencias, que te lleva a casa; lo que te asustó fue el silencio; reflexión: pedir ayuda no es debilidad. Incluye gancho, tensión, giro, énfasis (cleft o inversión) y reflexión final.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión añade tensión antes del giro?

choices.text: The station was silent. Then I heard footsteps, and I did not look back.
I was very scared. Then I saw my teacher.
My teacher came, and I was not scared.

feedback.es: La versión con la pista de los pasos y la reacción del narrador crea tensión porque retrasa la explicación. La frase simple revela todo de inmediato.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál es el giro de la historia.

choices.text: The neighbour really disliked the narrator.
The neighbour who seemed unfriendly had been in hospital.
The narrator never sent any messages.

feedback.es: El narrador creía que la vecina lo ignoraba, pero ella estaba en el hospital: ese cambio de sentido es el giro de la historia.

origin.audio: For weeks I thought my neighbour disliked me because she never answered my messages. Then I learned that she had been in hospital all that time.
